facts: Q1 2026 global billings of $383 million declined 1% year-over-year, slightly below guidance, while revenue was flat at $117 million and adjusted EBITDA of $12.8 million came in slightly below the guided range.

Adjusted EBITDA of $12.8 million included approximately $2 million of severance expense in SG&A tied to a roughly 5% headcount reduction executed in Q1, which was not added back to the non-GAAP figure.

Management is evaluating additional Q2 restructuring expected to reduce global headcount by approximately another 15%, along with further cost reduction and automation actions, though not yet Board-approved.

Groupon repurchased 2.8 million shares for $29.7 million at a weighted average price of $10.58 since the March 10 earnings release, representing roughly 7% of shares outstanding, with approximately $215 million remaining under authorization as of May 7.
Full-year 2026 guidance was affirmed at billings growth of 3%-5%, revenue of $513-$523 million, adjusted EBITDA of $70-$75 million, and free cash flow of at least $60 million.
Q2 2026 guidance calls for billings flat to up 2%, revenue of $126-$128 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $13-$15 million, kept in line with Q1 due to tough enterprise comparisons later in the quarter.

North America local decelerated as SMB merchant acquisition slowed and enterprise turned negative for the first time in 5 quarters, and health/beauty/wellness posted its first soft quarter after 4 consecutive quarters of growth.
April performance improved with North America local reaccelerating, email returning to positive year-over-year growth, and SEO trajectory turning positive in mid-April.
Management targets having the majority of new SMB merchant meetings set by AI voice agents by the end of 2026, and expects every Groupon leader to be using AI agents in daily work by the end of Q2.

Groupon retains a minority stake in SumUp, which it views as non-core and intends to monetize opportunistically if a liquidity event occurs, with proceeds to be deployed via its existing capital allocation framework including buybacks.
Total revenue for Q3 2025 was $294 million, a decrease of 10% compared to the prior quarter.
Adjusted EBITDA totaled $35 million, representing 12% of revenue and a 29% decrease from the prior quarter.
Free cash flow for the completions business was $25 million in Q3 2025.
The company now has 7 contracted frac fleets, with approximately 70% of active hydraulic horsepower committed under long-term contracts.
ProPetro secured a $350 million leasing facility letter of intent with an investment-grade partner to help fund PROPWR growth.
The company has over 150 megawatts contracted with expectations to reach at least 220 megawatts contracted by year-end 2025.
PROPWR equipment total cost, including balance of plant, is estimated to average approximately $1.1 million per megawatt.
Total liquidity at the end of Q3 2025 was $158 million, including $67 million in cash and $91 million of available capacity under the ABL credit facility.
The company anticipates full-year 2025 capital expenditures incurred to be between $270 million and $290 million, down from the prior $270 million to $310 million guidance.
ProPetro expects to maintain 10 to 11 active frac fleets in Q4 2025 and sustain at least this level of activity into 2026 under current market conditions.
AMC Networks generated $232 million in free cash flow in the first nine months of 2025 and is on track to achieve approximately $250 million for the full year.
Streaming revenue grew 14% year-over-year in Q3, while affiliate revenue declined 13%, resulting in flat overall subscription revenue.
The company ended Q3 with 10.4 million streaming subscribers, representing 2% year-over-year growth.
Digital advertising commitments increased 40% in the finalized upfront negotiations.
Consolidated net revenue declined 6% year-over-year to $562 million in Q3, while consolidated AOI declined 28% to $94 million.
Net debt stands at approximately $1.2 billion with a consolidated net leverage ratio of 2.8x and approximately $900 million of total liquidity.
More than 850,000 Spectrum customers have opted into AMC+ since its inclusion in Charter video packages earlier this year.
Domestic content licensing revenue is now expected to exceed $250 million for the full year.

The company repurchased $9 million of unsecured senior notes due 2029 at an average price of $0.84 on the dollar in Q3 and paid down approximately $166 million of Term Loan A subsequent to quarter end.
Globally, AMC Networks has 33 FAST channels distributed across 22 platforms totaling 215 active channel feeds as of the end of September.
Q2 revenue grew 8% to $1.08 billion and non-GAAP EPS rose 26% to $1.21, marking the tenth consecutive quarter of beating consensus earnings expectations.

Cooper has reached settlements with over 95% of claimants in the December 2023 embryo culture media recall litigation, taking a $271.6 million net charge ($324.1M accrued settlements offset by $52.5M insurance recoveries), with most payouts expected in fiscal 2026.

The strategic review has advanced with multiple parties submitting significant indications of interest in CooperSurgical, and management is proceeding with offers for the entire business rather than piecemeal, with a definitive update expected potentially before the September earnings call.

Full-year CooperVision organic growth guidance was lowered to 3.5%–4.5% (from prior expectations) due to Asia Pac market weakness, particularly consumer softness in Japan and China, while CooperSurgical guidance is unchanged at 4%–5% organic growth.

Asia Pac CooperVision revenue declined 6% in Q2 and is expected to decline again in Q3 against a -5% comp, with management expecting the region to return to in-line-with-market growth by Q4 and through 2027.
Full-year EPS guidance was maintained at $4.58–$4.66 despite an $0.11 Q2 beat, as FX is expected to swing from a tailwind in H1 to a meaningful headwind in H2.
Q3 gross margin is expected to be approximately 66%, pressured by unfavorable FX, tariffs, freight, and lower CooperVision production tied to a new AI-enabled inventory reduction initiative.

2026 free cash flow guidance was raised to roughly $650 million (excluding litigation payouts), and the company reiterated a $2.2 billion cumulative free cash flow target for 2026–2028 inclusive of expected litigation payouts.

Share repurchases were limited to $13 million in Q2 due to restrictions tied to other activity, but management indicated buybacks will be significantly more active going forward, with proceeds from any CooperSurgical transaction largely directed to buybacks.

Fertility grew 10% organically to $144 million driven by capital equipment strength and Middle East distributor restocking, but H2 fertility growth is expected to moderate to mid-single digits, while MiSight grew 24% to $32 million and PARAGARD was flat versus a tough comp, exceeding expectations.
Q3 2025 revenue was $681 million, up 6% sequentially and at the high end of prior guidance, representing a return to year-over-year growth.
Non-GAAP EPS of $0.62 was at the high point of prior guidance range of $0.56 to $0.62.
Q3 marked the eighth consecutive quarter of 10% or greater gross margin, with non-GAAP gross margin at 10.1%.
The company generated $25 million in free cash flow in Q3 and more than $74 million over the last 12 months.
Cash conversion cycle improved to 77 days, down 8 days sequentially and 13 days year-over-year, with inventory turns reaching 4.8.
Medical revenue grew 15% sequentially and 18% year-over-year, while A&D revenue increased 2% sequentially and 26% year-over-year.
Q4 2025 guidance projects revenue of $670 million to $720 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.62 to $0.68, representing mid-single digit year-over-year growth at the midpoint.
The company repurchased $10 million in stock and distributed $6 million in cash dividends during Q3, with approximately $124 million remaining in share repurchase authorization.
Semi-cap demand is expected to strengthen in the second half of 2026 with potential acceleration as the year progresses, according to customer conversations.
Cash balance was $286 million at quarter end with a liquidity ratio of 0.2x, down from 0.7x in the prior year period.
Q4 FY26 revenue was approximately $203 million, down 1% year-over-year from $205 million, reflecting timing-related order shifts that pulled certain Q4 orders into Q3, with diluted EPS flat at $0.52.
Full fiscal year 2026 revenue grew 4.5% to $859.5 million and diluted EPS rose nearly 12% to $2.48, exceeding the high end of guidance.

FY27 guidance calls for revenue of $885 million to $915 million and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.65 to $2.80, with Q1 FY27 revenue expected to grow mid-single digits and EPS growing at approximately twice that rate.

NetScout completed a tuck-in acquisition of DigiCert's DDoS protection business (closed May 1), expected to be immediately accretive with an initial annualized revenue run rate of approximately $20 million.
Cybersecurity revenue grew approximately 8% in FY26 (36% of total revenue) while Service Assurance grew approximately 3% (64% of revenue), with Enterprise up 5.4% and Service Provider up 3.3%.
Full-year gross margin rose 0.8 percentage points to 80.8% and operating margin expanded 1.7 percentage points to 25.4%, driven by favorable product mix and disciplined cost management.

Total product backlog grew to approximately $50 million (including $45.8 million fulfillable) versus $33 million ($25.1 million fulfillable) a year ago, attributed to order timing rather than supply chain constraints.

FY26 free cash flow reached a near-record $285.4 million ($150.1 million in Q4), and cash and marketable securities increased $212.7 million to $705.1 million with no balance drawn on the $600 million revolving credit facility.
The company repurchased approximately 2.5 million shares at an average price of $24.29 for roughly $61 million in FY26 and intends to remain active in buybacks during FY27.

Q4 wins included a mid-seven-figure DDoS upgrade deal with a large European telecom and a low-seven-figure new-customer deal with a global chip manufacturer; the new Omnis sensor/streamer product generated $10–$15 million in FY26 (mostly second half).
Q1 2026 sales grew 9.5% year-over-year to $521.7 million, with sales per business day rising from $7.57 million to $8.28 million.

Gross margins expanded ~79 basis points year-over-year to 32.3%, while adjusted EBITDA was $57.8 million at an 11.1% margin and adjusted diluted EPS came in at $1.26 (GAAP EPS $1.22 vs. $1.39 in Q4 2025).

Innovative Pumping Solutions sales surged 37.7% year-over-year to $111.7 million, with DXP Water comprising 66% of IPS sales and the segment marking its 14th consecutive quarter of sequential water sales growth.
Service Centers grew only 3.3% year-over-year and declined 5.1% sequentially, while Supply Chain Services grew 2.7% year-over-year and 6.2% sequentially.
Monthly average daily sales accelerated meaningfully: $7.2M in January, $8.4M in February, $9.2M in March, and $9.0M in April—with April up 15% year-over-year.

SG&A increased $16.1 million year-over-year to $126.1 million (24.2% of sales), driven partly by elevated healthcare claims, legal/audit costs from acquisitions, and one-time fleet/equipment expenses management views as non-recurring.
Free cash flow was $26.3 million and operating cash flow $29.6–29.8 million, while CapEx fell to $3.3 million (less than 1% of sales), down $16.6 million from Q1 2025.

Acquisitions completed in the past year contributed $40.7 million of Q1 sales; DXP closed three deals in Q1 (Mid Atlantic Storage Systems, PREMIERflow, Ambiente H2O), has 3 more under LOI and 2 close to LOI.

Cash declined $90.4 million sequentially to $213.4 million due to acquisition spending, total debt stood at $844.7 million, secured leverage ratio was 2.6x on covenant LTM EBITDA of $243.9 million, and liquidity totaled $366.7 million.

ROIC reached 34.1%, interest expense rose $1.8 million year-over-year following a fall refinancing that added $205 million in incremental debt, and energy-related backlog grew 2.1% sequentially, reversing declines from Q3/Q4 2025.
Full year 2025 revenue grew 13% year-over-year to $183.6 million, exceeding the 5% midpoint of initial full year guidance, with 10% growth excluding ResMetrics' $5.2 million contribution.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA increased 20% year-over-year to $26.7 million with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.5%, up from 13.7% in 2024.
Free cash flow after distributions to noncontrolling interest totaled $18.9 million in 2025, representing over 70% adjusted EBITDA to free cash flow conversion.

The company ended 2025 with $36.7 million in cash, total debt of $7.6 million (entirely finance leases), resulting in a net positive cash position of $29.1 million and total liquidity of approximately $61 million.
Full year 2026 revenue guidance is $184 million to $194 million with adjusted EBITDA expected between $26 million and $29 million, with earnings and cash flow weighted toward the second half.

Q4 2025 revenue was $50.6 million, up 13% year-over-year and 9% sequentially, with U.S. revenue increasing 69% year-over-year driven by improved fracturing system sales, higher plug revenue, and a $2.9 million ResMetrics contribution.
Q4 2025 net income included a $9.8 million positive impact from the release of deferred tax valuation allowances, contributing to full year diluted EPS of $8.65 compared to $2.55 in 2024.
Q1 2026 revenue guidance is $49 million to $53 million, implying approximately 2% growth at the midpoint versus Q1 2025, with adjusted EBITDA expected between $6.5 million and $8.5 million.
The company expects 2026 free cash flow after distributions of $12 million to $16 million, with the midpoint representing a free cash flow yield of approximately 13% to market capitalization.

The company targets incremental adjusted EBITDA margins of 25% to 35% over time and has set a medium-term return on invested capital objective of 15%, having achieved after-tax returns of over 11% in 2025.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 41% year-over-year to $8 million in fiscal Q2 2026, despite revenue increasing only 2%.
Total revenues were $20.7 million in fiscal Q2 2026, up 2% year-over-year, driven by a 6% increase in production and higher realized natural gas prices offset by lower oil and NGL pricing.
Net income was $1.1 million or $0.03 per diluted share compared to a net loss of $1.8 million or $0.06 per share in the year-ago period.
Lease operating expenses improved to $16.96 per BOE compared to $20.05 per BOE in the prior year quarter, reflecting mineral/royalty acquisitions and cessation of CO2 purchases at Delhi.

As of December 31, 2025, cash on hand was $3.8 million, borrowings under the credit facility were $54.5 million, and total liquidity increased to approximately $13.5 million versus $11.9 million last quarter.
The Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.12 per share, with $4.2 million in total dividends paid during the quarter.

Newly acquired Haynesville-Bossier Shale mineral and royalty assets had essentially zero impact on the just-ended quarter, with less than $1 million of the approximately $4 million acquisition cost spent in fiscal Q2 and the majority expected in fiscal Q3.

At Chaveroo, the transition from electric submersible pumps to rod pumps on all but two wells improved lifting efficiency and resulted in field performance trending about 5% above initial expectations.

At TexMex, 14 workovers were completed during the quarter at a cost of a couple hundred thousand dollars net, adding approximately 80 net barrels of oil per day, with only 4 additional workovers currently identified going forward.

Management maintained full-year capital expenditure guidance of $4 million to $6 million and stated a long-term target of 1x net debt leverage, acknowledging current levels are somewhat above that target.'
Q2 fiscal 2026 sales of approximately $6.3 billion exceeded the high end of guidance, up 12% year-over-year and 7% sequentially.
Adjusted diluted earnings per share of $1.05 exceeded the high end of guidance, growing nearly 4x faster than sales compared to last quarter.
Asia sales reached a record high of over $3 billion, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of year-on-year sales growth in the region.
The company generated $208 million of cash flow from operations in Q2 and reduced inventory by $126 million or 2.3% sequentially.
Electronic Components operating margin was 3.2% and Farnell operating margin was 4.7%, with Farnell achieving its highest operating margin since fiscal 2023.
Q3 fiscal 2026 guidance projects sales of $6.2 billion to $6.5 billion and diluted EPS of $1.20 to $1.30.
Gross leverage ended Q2 at 3.9x with approximately $1.7 billion of available committed borrowing capacity, with management anticipating reducing leverage to approximately 3x over the next year.
Return on working capital improved over 100 basis points compared to last quarter through operating income growth and reduction in working capital days.
Farnell sales increased 24% year-over-year (20% in constant currency) and 7% sequentially.
The Americas region remains approximately 20-25% below historical peak sales levels and Europe remains approximately 30-35% below peak levels, representing significant recovery potential.

DoorDash's Q2 2026 gas rewards/driver support program is expected to impact results by approximately $50 million, similar to the $50 million impact in Q1, with the company offsetting it by pushing some H1 investments into H2.

Management reiterated that full-year 2026 EBITDA margins are expected to be slightly higher than 2025 excluding GOV, with GOV expected to produce roughly $200 million of EBITDA, and H2 EBITDA dollars and margins expected to exceed H1.
Winter storms negatively impacted Q1 GOV growth by roughly 1 percentage point year-over-year.
DoorDash reported MAUs reached an all-time high, with subscription posting a record quarter across DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt, and member growth accelerating year-over-year.

Deliveroo is delivering its highest growth rate in the past four years and has been reaccelerating each month under DoorDash ownership, while Wolt has reached its highest share performance in each country it operates in.
Approximately two-thirds of DoorDash's code is now written by AI, and management expects near-term OpEx growth to remain in the roughly 2% range.
DoorDash captures about 1 in every 2 new consumers entering the grocery delivery industry for the first time, and became the volume share leader in grocery in late 2025/early 2026.

The new vertical portfolio is on track to be gross profit positive in the second half of 2026, with about 30% of monthly active users currently ordering from non-restaurant categories (vs. a long-term target of 100%).

The global tech replatforming involves running all three tech stacks (DoorDash, Wolt, Deliveroo) in parallel, with the majority of redundant costs running through 2026 and some bleeding into early 2027 before phasing out.

Management confirmed the autonomous delivery platform 'Dot' has launched in a couple of markets with early results meeting plan, framing 2026 as a year focused on hardening autonomy, hardware, remote operations, and regulatory scale capabilities.
Q3 2025 revenue was $809 million with core revenue down 10% year-over-year, driven by lower volumes in both North America and Europe.
Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 was $44 million (5.5% of sales), a decline of approximately $38 million from the prior year.
Net debt leverage increased to 7.4x, driven by lower year-over-year EBITDA rather than new borrowing.
The company announced an approximately 11% reduction in North America and corporate headcount, expected to deliver roughly $50 million in full year savings in 2026.
Full year 2025 guidance was lowered to sales of $3.1-$3.2 billion (from $3.2-$3.4 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $105-$120 million (from $170-$200 million).
The company initiated a strategic review of its European business to evaluate alternatives to strengthen the balance sheet and address elevated leverage.
Liquidity position remains at approximately $500 million ($100 million cash plus $400 million revolver availability) with no debt maturities until December 2027.
North America revenue declined 19% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA falling to $38 million from $75 million in the prior year quarter.
Annualized tariff impact is estimated at approximately $45 million, with roughly $17 million expected to materialize in 2025 results.
Operating cash flow guidance was revised to a use of approximately $45 million compared to prior forecast of a $10 million use, and CapEx was reduced to approximately $125 million from $150 million.
Air Group reported a Q1 2026 GAAP net loss of $193 million and an adjusted net loss of $192 million ($1.68 adjusted loss per share), better than the midpoint of revised guidance.

Q1 fuel costs were more than $100 million higher than expected (~$0.70 EPS impact), and management expects incremental fuel costs of $600 million or more in Q2 (~$3.60 EPS impact), with Q2 EPS guided to a loss of approximately $1 per share.
Q1 total revenues reached $3.3 billion, up 5% year-over-year on capacity growth of 1.7%, with unit revenues up 3.5%.
Hawaii storms and Puerto Vallarta civil unrest—regions representing ~30% of system capacity—reduced Q1 unit revenues by nearly 1 point, prompting a ~30% reduction in Puerto Vallarta flying for Q2.
Management expects a path to Q2 system unit revenues up 10% (high single digits base case) despite a 2-point Hawaii drag, with Continental U.S. incoming yields up 20%+ year-over-year recently.

A multi-year extension with Bank of America secures an additional $1 billion of cash remuneration through 2030, adding ~0.5 point of margin in 2026 and a full point in 2027, incremental to the prior $150 million loyalty profit target by 2027.
Q1 generated $615 million in cash remuneration from co-brand cards (up 12% YoY) with Atmos active membership up 13%; Hawaii-based cardholder spend rose 19% YoY, representing nearly 6% of state GDP.
Liquidity stands at ~$2.9 billion with $20 billion in unencumbered assets, net leverage of 3.3x, debt-to-capital of 61%; $340 million of debt was repaid in Q1 with $65 million expected in Q2.
Year-to-date share repurchases reached $250 million with $180 million remaining under the $1 billion authorization, but further buybacks are paused to evaluate the outlook.

Q1 unit costs rose 6.3% YoY; Q2 CASM-ex is expected ~1.5 points above Q1 due to transitory items, with CASM-ex inflecting down to low single digits in H2 2026, and management reiterated conviction in the long-term $10 EPS target while suspending full-year guidance.
Humana reported 2025 adjusted EPS of $17.14, above initial guidance of approximately $16.25.
Humana expects 2026 full year adjusted EPS of at least $9, with the decline driven by a Bonus Year 2026 Stars headwind.
The net Stars headwind for 2026, including individual and group MA, is approximately $3.5 billion.
Humana grew by approximately 1 million members or 20% in AEP and anticipates full year 2026 individual MA membership growth of approximately 25%.
Despite expected premium growth of 40% from 2024 to 2026, statutory capital requirements will increase by less than 20%, offsetting over $3 billion of growth in capital requirements.
Over 70% of new sales were switchers from competitor plans, and nearly 30% of new sales were bounce-back members previously enrolled with Humana.

Individual MA margins in 2026 are expected to be slightly below breakeven after accounting for the Stars headwind, but normalizing for Stars, individual MA margin is expected to double year-over-year.
Approximately 90% of the incremental investments made in 2025 (estimated at over $550 million) were attributed to medical costs.
The full year 2025 insurance segment benefit ratio of 90.4% came in slightly better than guidance.
Humana's value-based care mix remains approximately one-third in full risk, one-third in other value-based arrangements, and one-third in non-value-based or basic pay-for-performance models.
Q3 2025 revenue grew 14.5% year-over-year to $339 million, consistent with the prior quarter's growth rate.
Non-GAAP operating margin reached 17% in Q3, up 380 basis points quarter-over-quarter, though this included some onetime G&A benefits from facility and tax reimbursements.
The number of 6- and 7-figure deals accelerated to 31% year-over-year growth, with customers generating $100,000+ ARR now totaling more than 2,600.
Current RPO (cRPO) grew 23% year-over-year, primarily benefiting from longer average contract durations that increased further in Q3.
Net new ARR growth came in notably faster than revenue growth in Q3, with management reiterating confidence in their base case growth trajectory.
Procore announced a new $300 million stock repurchase program for one year after the prior authorization expired, following $129 million in repurchases year-to-date representing 1.9 million shares.
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance was raised to $1.312-$1.314 billion (14% growth) and non-GAAP operating margin guidance was raised to 14%, implying 400 basis points of year-over-year expansion.
Ajei Gopal will become CEO on November 10, 2025, succeeding founder Tooey Courtemanche who will transition to Chair of the Board.
Procore surpassed $1 trillion in annual construction volume contracted to its platform, up from approximately $900 billion at the November 2024 Investor Day.
Half of Procore's top 10 new logo deals in Q3 involved no other vendor in the prospect's evaluation, demonstrating uncontested category leadership.

Q1 2026 total revenues declined to $353 million from $380.6 million in Q1 2025, with residential video down ~$10 million and residential data down $11.6 million (5.1%) driven by a 6.1% subscriber decline.
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $183.3 million (51.9% margin) from $202.7 million (53.3% margin) a year earlier, while free cash flow was $114.9 million versus $131.6 million in Q1 2025.

Residential broadband subscribers declined by 12,600 sequentially in Q1, with churn concentrated in the ~15% of the footprint considered hypercompetitive, though gross connects improved year-over-year.
Management expects back-book ARPU to need adjustment of roughly $2 to $5 over a multi-year period to reach competitive parity, while still guiding ARPU to remain broadly stable for full-year 2026.

The company repaid $575 million of maturing convertible notes via revolver draw, and paid down an additional $90.6 million of debt ($86.1 million voluntary) including senior notes and term loans at attractive discounts.
Net leverage stood at 4.0x on an LQA basis with $3.1 billion of total debt, $165.6 million of cash, and $700 million of undrawn revolver capacity at quarter-end.

The MBI acquisition purchase price remains locked at $480 million with closing expected at the beginning of Q4 2026, but assumed/refinanced debt range was raised to $895–$925 million due to MBI's weaker 2025 performance.
MBI lost just under 2,000 net broadband subscribers in Q1 2026, a meaningful improvement from its 2025 run rate, and post-close leverage is expected to exceed the previously stated ~4x target.

The company sold certain fiber-to-the-tower contract rights in mid-March for $42 million in cash, recognizing a $26.6 million gain; those contracts generated $9 million of business data revenue in 2025 and $2.1 million in Q1.

Approximately 53% of markets are currently multi-gig capable with plans to expand to most markets by year-end, and a new CRM platform supporting retention initiatives is expected to go live later this year.
The Phase III ANCHOR trial was initiated six months earlier than originally planned, triggering a $45 million milestone payment to J&J booked in Q3 2025 but payable in Q4.
FDA feedback expanded the eligible patient population for CD388 from 50 million to over 100 million people in the U.S. by including healthy adults over 65.
The Phase III ANCHOR study is over 50% enrolled and on track to achieve target enrollment of 6,000 participants across 150 sites in the Northern Hemisphere by December.
Cidara received a BARDA award valued up to $339 million, with a base period of $58 million over 24 months to support manufacturing onshoring and clinical development.
The company reported approximately $476 million in cash at September 30, 2025, which fully funds the Phase III program through completion in all scenarios.
The Phase IIb NAVIGATE study demonstrated that a single 450-milligram dose of CD388 provided 76.1% protective efficacy extending through the entire flu season.
The FDA granted CD388 breakthrough therapy designation in early October 2025, in addition to its existing fast track status.
An interim analysis is expected in late Q1 2026 to assess trial size, powering assumptions, and event rate to determine if Southern Hemisphere enrollment is necessary.
WuXi manufacturing capacity will provide approximately 5 million doses per year at the 450-milligram dose level for initial commercial launch.
The company is targeting a BLA filing in 2027, with CMC qualification requirements being the rate-limiting factor for the regulatory submission.
Pool Corporation reported Q3 2025 net sales of $1.5 billion, up 1% year-over-year.
Gross margin expanded 50 basis points to 29.6% in Q3, driven by favorable pricing, supply chain initiatives, and private label sales growth.
Building materials sales increased 4% in Q3, marking the first year-over-year growth in that category since Q3 2022.
POOL360 digital platform adoption reached an all-time high of 17% of total sales in Q3.
Diluted EPS increased 4% to $3.40 in Q3, compared to $3.27 in the prior year period.
The company confirmed full-year diluted EPS guidance of $10.81 to $11.31, including $0.11 in realized ASU tax benefits year-to-date.
Total chemical sales declined 4% in Q3, reflecting deflation particularly in trichlor sanitizers which were down mid-to-high single digits.
Cash flow from operations was $286 million year-to-date versus $487 million in the prior year, with the decrease primarily due to higher tax payments and working capital investments.
The company completed $184 million in share repurchases through the earnings call date, with $493 million remaining under the authorization.
Operating expenses increased 5% in Q3, including accelerated technology investments and costs from new greenfield locations not open in both periods.
Q3 2025 revenue reached $585 million, up 68% year-over-year, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of more than 60% revenue growth.
Reddit achieved a 40% adjusted EBITDA margin in Q3, meeting the profitability target set at the company's IPO just 18 months prior.
Q4 2025 guidance projects revenue of $655 million to $665 million (53-55% year-over-year growth) and adjusted EBITDA of $275 million to $285 million with a 42% margin at midpoint.
Advertising revenue grew 74% year-over-year to $549 million, with total active advertiser count expanding by over 75% year-over-year.
Daily active unique users (DAUq) reached 116 million and weekly active unique users (WAUq) hit 444 million, both growing approximately 20% year-over-year.
GAAP net income was $163 million with a 28% net margin, an improvement of $133 million from the prior year.
Average revenue per user (ARPU) grew 41% year-over-year to $5.04, which management noted remains low on an absolute basis and represents an opportunity.
Free cash flow for Q3 was $183 million (31% margin), and the company has generated over $500 million of free cash flow in the last 12 months with $2.2 billion in cash on the balance sheet.
Stock-based compensation as a percentage of revenue decreased from 19% to 16% sequentially, while total fully diluted shares outstanding declined to 206.1 million from 206.6 million last quarter.
Nine of Reddit's top 15 advertising verticals grew revenues by 50% or more, with both performance ads and brand ads growing more than 70% year-over-year.
OCU400 Phase III liMeliGhT trial enrollment is complete with 140 patients randomized 2:1 into treatment and untreated control groups, with top line data expected in Q1 2027.
Rolling BLA submission for OCU400 is planned to begin in Q3 2026, with anticipated commercialization in 2027.

OCU410 Phase II ArMaDa trial showed a 46% reduction in lesion growth at 12 months across medium and high dose groups combined versus control with statistical significance at p=0.015 in a cohort of 23 patients.
Currently marketed GA products demonstrated only a 22% lesion reduction at 2 years, while OCU410 showed 46% reduction at just 1 year, more than double the benefit in half the time.
Current cash and cash equivalents extend the company's runway into Q4 2026, and if $30 million in warrants from a prior Janus Henderson raise are exercised in full, runway extends into Q2 2027.
Full year 2025 R&D expenses were $39.8 million compared to $32.1 million in 2024, and net loss per share was $0.23 compared to $0.20 in the prior year.
The company raised $22.5 million through an underwritten registered direct offering of common stock led by RTW Investments.
